title: What is the area of a rhombus with diagonals 20 cm and 15 cm?
description: A rhombus has diagonals of twenty and fifteen centimetres. The rhombus becomes a rectangle as long as one diagonal and half as wide as the other, and the area follows from its sides.
teaching_notes: One idea: the area of a rhombus is half of one diagonal times the other. Watch for students who forget the half.

source: Figure it Out (rhombus and trapezium, question 1)
video_script.why: The child uses the rectangle made from a rhombus in the solved example to find the area from the two diagonals.
video_script.substitution: Make the rectangle one diagonal long and half the other wide, then multiply.
video_script.anchor: the book's rhombus with diagonals 20 cm and 15 cm
video_script.payoff_line: The area of the rhombus is one hundred and fifty square centimetres

final_answer.spoken: one hundred and fifty square centimetres

maths_rules: rhombus with diagonals 20 cm and 15 cm
the rectangle is 20 cm by 15 ÷ 2 = 7.5 cm
video_script.design: One rhombus all video: the rectangle from its diagonals, then a check with half of the diagonals multiplied.

narration: <bookmark mark='diag'/>The diagonals of a rhombus cross at a right angle, and each cuts the other in half.
<bookmark mark='rect'/>Cutting along them rearranges the rhombus into a rectangle.
<bookmark mark='sides'/>That rectangle is one whole diagonal long and half the other diagonal wide.

beats.on_screen: Given: rhombus ABCD, diagonals AC = 20 cm and BD = 15 cm
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a rhombus with diagonals of twenty centimetres and fifteen centimetres.

beats.on_screen: To find: the area of the rhombus

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the area of the rhombus.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the rectangle has length AC = 20 and breadth BD ÷ 2 = 15 ÷ 2 = 7.5
narration: <bookmark mark='len'/>Step one, the rectangle is as long as the whole diagonal of twenty.
<bookmark mark='wid'/>Its breadth is half of the other diagonal. Half of fifteen is seven point five.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: area of the rhombus = area of the rectangle = 20 × 7.5 = 150

marks.same: an equals sign appears between the rhombus and the rectangle

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step two, the rhombus has the same area as the rectangle.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Twenty times seven point five gives one hundred and fifty square centimetres.
<bookmark mark='chk'/>Step three, check it. Half of twenty times fifteen is half of three hundred.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Half of three hundred is also one hundred and fifty.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The area of the rhombus is one hundred and fifty square centimetres.
